# Authorized Roles {.unnumbered}

There are two types of roles a person may be authorized with on Databrary, **Authorized Investigator** or **Sponsored Researcher**. 

## Authorized Investigator

### What is an Authorized Investigator?

An Authorized Investigator is typically a person who has PI status or equivalent at their institution. On Databrary, Authorized Investigators have the ability to authorize research staff, post-docs, or students as Sponsored Researchers. They have the ability to create volumes, manage collaborators on their volumes, and share their volume publicly on Databrary.

### Eligibility

Databrary policies and your home institution determine whether you are eligible to be granted access to Databrary as an Authorized Investigator. To be eligible as a Databrary Authorized Investigator, you must meet these criteria: 

- I conduct independent, unsupervised, research at my institution;
- I submit funding proposals as lead investigator;
- I have Principal Investigator (PI) status or hold a tenure-track faculty position at my institution;
- My institution maintains or uses an ethics board to review and approve research involving human subjects (or non-human animals where relevant);
- I have current training that addresses research ethics with human subjects (e.g. CITI training);
- I would like to reuse or upload data to Databrary.
- I sponsor and supervise lab staff and students who work on my projects or on collaborative projects, and I have authority to supervise their access to data that I share or others have shared on Databrary.

### Seeking Authorization
If these criteria apply to you, you can find more information [here.](authorized-researchers.qmd)

## Sponsored Researcher

### What is a Sponsored Researcher?

::: {.callout-note}

Sponsored Researchers are currently referred to as "Affiliates" on Databrary. By August 2026, the term "Affiliates" will be removed and changed to  "Sponsored Researchers". 

:::

A Sponsored Researcher is typically a student or research staff who conducts research under a research supervisor. On Databrary, Sponsored Researchers have the ability to edit their Authorized Investigator's volumes, as well as any volumes that they are added as a collaborator. 

::: {.callout-note}

In some cases, a Sponsored Researcher may be able to create volumes if their Authorized Investigator upgrades their account privileges.  

:::

### Eligibility

Databrary policies, your home institution, and the Authorized Investigator who supervises your research determines whether you are eligible to be granted access to Databrary as a Sponsored Researcher. To be eligible as a Databrary Sponsored Researcher, you must meet these criteria:

- I conduct research under the supervision of an Authorized Investigator’s sponsorship or someone who is eligible to become an Authorized Investigator;
- I am a student, research staff, or post-doctoral researcher.
- I have current training that addresses research ethics with human subjects (e.g.[CITI training](https://about.citiprogram.org/)).

Before you can be authorized as a Sponsored Researcher, your research supervisor must be authorized as an Authorized Investigator on Databrary. 

### Seeking Authorization
If these criteria apply to you, you can find more information [here.](sponsored-researchers.qmd)
